claims.author: sedited
claims.question: why is custom functionality introduced for findBlock and how to validate changes without tests
claims.quote: why is so much custom functionality introduced for `findBlock`?

status_by.quote: Chain::findBlock and the handful of other Chain methods taking FoundBlock input/output arguments need custom code because these are converted to FoundBlockParam and FoundBlockResult Cap'n Proto structs to make IPC calls, and these structs are recursive

claims.status_note: author explained recursive structs require custom capnp translation code

claims.author: sedited
claims.question: whether Data blobs and enums should be strongly typed in capnp for non-C++ clients

claims.harm: missing struct fields like best_height in estimateSmartFee and mismatched integer and enum types lead to serialization bugs and compilation issues
claims.quote: It seems to me the capnp wrapper needs some updates (missing field, 32/64 bit params, param rename, bool vs uint64, enums as unsigned, optional mapping, unused declarations, comments, etc).

claims.author: xyzconstant
claims.question: whether ChainClient should be reduced to lifecycle and mock-time hooks and the rest moved to WalletLoader
claims.quote: Would it be worth reducing `ChainClient` to just lifecycle + mock-time hooks and moving the rest to `WalletLoader`?

status_by.quote: I get it now, thanks you!

claims.status_note: reviewer accepted author explanation that ChainClient is designed for node-spawned processes

claims.author: willcl-ark
claims.harm: node could hit undefined behavior when switching on broadcastmethod without safe enum mapping or a default case
claims.quote: broadcastmethod is switched on (e.g. here) with no default case, as is our convention. but we don't check incoming value is mapped to the enum safely.

status_by.quote: In C++, the compiler enforces at each call site that explicit values need to be passed for all parameters which don't have defaults.

claims.status_note: author explained C++ callers enforce explicit values, and non-C++ callers must handle omitted values safely

claims.author: willcl-ark
claims.quote: even though these are positional, I think we can rename descendants -> cluster_count post-cluster mempool (and as this is public facing).
claims.request: rename descendants parameter to cluster_count post-cluster mempool

status_by.quote: Good catch. It looks like the parameter was renamed in commit 957ae232414b38adcf9358e198fded42f7c1feea and this PR was not updated.

claims.status_note: author confirmed the parameter was renamed upstream and agreed it should be updated

claims.author: willcl-ark
claims.harm: node segfaults if a non-C++ client passes null transaction data or unhandled enum values over IPC
claims.quote: Also what happens here is tx is a null pointer (allowed by capnp spec AFAIU)? I think we will immediately try to deference it in BroadcastTransaction and segfault.

status_by.quote: This is a legitimate concern, and it's not specific to this method or to these parameters.

claims.status_note: author replied explaining that capnp allows null/defaults and discussed trade-offs and future mitigations

claims.author: willcl-ark
claims.question: why not omit ChainClient::start from the exposed interface or throw an exception rather than asserting
claims.quote: Why not omit start from the exposed base interface or make this throw a protocol error instead of asserting.

status_by.quote: This could throw an exception instead of assert. It shouldn't matter very much because I don't think there's a way this could be accidentally called.

claims.status_note: author explained libmultiprocess generation requirements and agreed an exception could be thrown instead
